cards.explanation: The answer is the Sabbath and the New Moon, friends. The Lord GOD says the gate stays shut during the six days of work, “…but on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened.” So the work week keeps it closed, and those two days are when it opens.

The answer is the priests, friends. The prince stands by the gatepost, and the priests are the ones who sacrifice his burnt offerings and peace offerings. Those offerings are his, but the sacrificing is theirs.
The answer is that he bows in worship, friends, right at the threshold of the gate. Then he departs. I think that's a humble way for a prince to head out the door.
The answer is False, friends. The prince bows and departs, but the gate stays open. The text says, “…but the gate must not be shut until evening.” (Ezekiel 46:2) No slamming it behind him.

The answer is the people of the land, friends. On Sabbaths and New Moons they also bow in worship before the LORD at the entrance to that gateway. So it's not just the prince bowing. Everybody gets to worship.

The answer is the south gate, friends. The text says whoever enters by the north gate must go out by the south gate. And it works the other way too: in by south, out by north. Everybody exits by the opposite gate.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, “When the people enter, the prince shall go in with them, and when they leave, he shall leave.” So he walks in with the crowd and walks out with the crowd. No sneaking out early for him.

The answer is True, friends. For the prince's freewill offering, “…the gate facing east must be opened for him.” He offers it just as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he goes out, and the gate is closed.

The answer is descendants, friends. If the prince gives a gift to one of his sons as an inheritance, it will belong to his descendants. It becomes their property by inheritance. So the gift stays in the family line.

The answer is that it goes back to the prince, friends. A gift from his inheritance to a servant belongs to that servant until the year of freedom. Then it reverts to the prince. A son's gift stays with the family line, but a servant's gift goes back.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, “The prince must not take any of the inheritance of the people by evicting them from their property.” He gives his sons an inheritance from his own property. The people's land is theirs.

The answer is so none of His people are displaced from their property, friends. That's the reason the Lord GOD gives. The prince provides for his sons from his own property, “…so that none of My people will be displaced from his property.” The rule is about the people staying put on their land.

The answer is cooking offerings, friends. The man says the priests will boil the guilt offering and the sin offering there, and bake the grain offering. It's a kitchen spot in the priests' holy chambers.

The answer is True, friends. The man says the priests cook those offerings there “…so that they do not bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.” So the cooking happens in the holy chambers. The outer court is kept clear of it.
